body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for The Crooked House: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: The crystal ball in the Parlour (Rook), the bergamot tree in the Conservatory (Tobin) and the stuffed Pomeranian and crow in the Trophy Room (Lucan) are those companions' own scenes: do not mention them. Lucan's hound is only called Dreadfang here. Do not describe the thing that haunts the house.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Tobin + Silas + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is on the hilltop grounds above the village, in the storm, before going into the house. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Druskenvald Estate: The hilltop grounds above Wickermoor Village: a gate in a fence, the pond, two barns, the kitchen gardens, a dead tree in the north-west corner, and the three-storey manor behind its wrap-around porch. Welcoming on the first night; ruined once the house turns. The hill road climbs to an open gate in an iron fence. Beyond it a pond lies black in a hollow, two barns lean together on a bench of level ground, and the house waits on the shoulder of the hill, its porch lit and every window wa... Parts of it: The gate; The wrap-around porch; The pond; The kitchen gardens; The barns' yard; The hill road; The dead tree. Things to see: The manor's front door; The open gate; The pond; The big barn; The small barn; The dead tree; A well; The porch steps; A rowboat drawn up on the bank. People here: Gilly Jenkin; Walter Jenkin.
EXCHANGE 2: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is on the ground floor of the bent manor. No séance has been held.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, First Floor: The ground floor of the Lockwood manor, bent out of true: a storm-lashed porch, a tall foyer with a curving stair, a parlor with a spirit board, a round gallery, a music room, a dining room laid for a feast, a wrecked kitchen and a glass conservatory. Rain drums on the porch. Inside, the floors lean, the doors sit in their frames at slight wrong angles, and every wall holds something that looks back. Parts of it: The dance floor; Porch; Foyer; Parlor; Gallery; Music Room; Dining Room; Kitchen. Things to see: The porch's edge, where the storm waits; A rocking chair; The Lockwood family portrait; The Druskenvalds' portrait; A portrait of your own party; A tilted chandelier; The curved stair; A compass rose inlaid in the floor; The round table and Adela's spirit board. People here: The Crooked Man; Petunia Lockwood.
EXCHANGE 3: Rook + Silas (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, silas_vane)
  Story now: The séance in the parlour has been held and the spirit board has said goodbye for good. The house is still haunted.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, First Floor: The ground floor of the Lockwood manor, bent out of true: a storm-lashed porch, a tall foyer with a curving stair, a parlor with a spirit board, a round gallery, a music room, a dining room laid for a feast, a wrecked kitchen and a glass conservatory. Rain drums on the porch. Inside, the floors lean, the doors sit in their frames at slight wrong angles, and every wall holds something that looks back. Parts of it: The dance floor; Porch; Foyer; Parlor; Gallery; Music Room; Dining Room; Kitchen. Things to see: The porch's edge, where the storm waits; A rocking chair; The Lockwood family portrait; The Druskenvalds' portrait; A portrait of your own party; A tilted chandelier; The curved stair; A compass rose inlaid in the floor; The round table and Adela's spirit board. People here: The Crooked Man; Petunia Lockwood.
EXCHANGE 4: Silas + Delphine (speaker ids: silas_vane, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come up to the second floor of the haunted house.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, Second Floor: The upper floor: a round sitting room in the turret, a children's room with two small beds, a red-stained bathroom, a master bedroom with a writhing bed, and a locked balcony over the porch. The upper hall slopes toward the turret. Doors stand ajar on rooms that were kept for children, a bath, and a bed that will not stay still. Parts of it: Sitting Room; Landing; Children's Room; Bathroom; Master Bedroom; The west hall; Balcony; The balcony's edge. Things to see: A grandfather clock, still ticking; A cracked rail over the foyer; A small bed; A second small bed; A dark window; A big toy chest; A child's armoire; A closet, ajar; A wooden doll.
EXCHANGE 5: Silas + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: Filthy Jasper has died in the master bedroom. The house is still haunted.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, Second Floor: The upper floor: a round sitting room in the turret, a children's room with two small beds, a red-stained bathroom, a master bedroom with a writhing bed, and a locked balcony over the porch. The upper hall slopes toward the turret. Doors stand ajar on rooms that were kept for children, a bath, and a bed that will not stay still. Parts of it: Sitting Room; Landing; Children's Room; Bathroom; Master Bedroom; The west hall; Balcony; The balcony's edge. Things to see: A grandfather clock, still ticking; A cracked rail over the foyer; A small bed; A second small bed; A dark window; A big toy chest; A child's armoire; A closet, ajar; A wooden doll.
EXCHANGE 6: Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come up to the top floor of the haunted house. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, Third Floor: The top floor: a nursery with a holed crib, a library of sagging shelves, and a trophy room of stuffed things in the wrong poses, with a stain on the ceiling that is a little too square. Wind finds its way into the top floor through places the walls swear are sealed. Books lie open on every flat thing, and the animals on the walls have all turned to watch the door. Parts of it: Nursery; The stair hall; The upper hall; Library; Trophy Room. Things to see: A mahogany crib riddled with tiny holes; A cradle, riddled the same way; A cobwebbed liquor cart; A tome left on a lectern; A desk under a stack of books; A square seam in the ceiling; A large brown bear, stuffed; A stuffed crow on a perch; The hearth, and the stained ceiling over it. People here: Arthur Lockwood.
EXCHANGE 7: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has reached the hidden attic.
  In front of them: The Crooked House, Attic: The hidden attic: a cramped landing cut with blood-red runes and six empty circles, a little warded door, and beyond it a long room whose floor is carpeted with teeth and whose cauldron bubbles red. The attic is a box of beams and red light. The runes pulse on every surface, and the air smells of hot copper and wet fur. Parts of it: Secret Landing; Cauldron Room; Round the cauldron. Things to see: Six empty circles in the runes; Blood-red runes; A great cauldron of glowing red ichor; Phillip, bound; Adela, bound; Scratchings in the beam; The round window. People here: Lady Adela Druskenvald; Phillip Druskenvald; Adela Druskenvald.
EXCHANGE 8: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: Vessla Browntooth is dead. The house has unbent, the storm has ended and the porch is open. The party stands on the grounds again. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Druskenvald Estate: The hilltop grounds above Wickermoor Village: a gate in a fence, the pond, two barns, the kitchen gardens, a dead tree in the north-west corner, and the three-storey manor behind its wrap-around porch. Beyond it a pond lies black in a hollow, two barns lean together on a bench of level ground, and the house waits on the shoulder of the hill, its porch lit and every window wa... THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY tobin_hayward: Look at those kitchen gardens, Silas, the rows are tidy enough, yet that dead tree in the corner has a canker right down to the taproot.
SAY silas_vane: Never mind the cabbages, Tobin, the whole manor's lit up like a riverside gaming hall and the front gate's standing wide open in a storm.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth by that black pond, friends. Dreadfang has his nose to the wet grass, and the spoor here smells of old pond-weed.
SAY tobin_hayward: Good soil, bad seed, Lucan, and my field mice just bolted down into my waistcoat. Something under this mud does not want to be dug up.
SAY silas_vane: When the house leaves the door unlatched and the lamps trimmed on a night like this, friend, the table's marked before you even sit down.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, not a single doorframe in this foyer sits on the true bias. Even the chandelier is leaning like a drunk in the cheap seats.
SAY cordelia_skein: It is the gallery that intrigues me, Delphine. Some thoughtful soul has hung a fresh portrait of our party, and the oil is still wonderfully tacky.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Oh, the brushwork on my button eye is pure slander, and Your Foolishness says the painter couldn't frame a joke, let alone a headliner.
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology in the parlour as well, darling. The dining room is laid for a banquet, yet the air tastes entirely of cold tallow and rot.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Every wall in this crooked box has eyes on it, Cordelia, and I do not care to perform for a house that already knows the curtain call.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY rook_coldwake: The spirit board on that parlour table is closed out, Silas, yet the floor slabs are still pitched four inches off level. The docket isn't clear.
SAY silas_vane: Tell's in the twitch, friend, and that rocking chair on the porch hasn't stopped moving since the little pointer slid over to goodbye.
SAY rook_coldwake: Unruly timber, that is. We had a polite word with the dead, logged the complaint, and the staircase is still groaning like a wet cellar.
SAY silas_vane: That's because the parlour ghost was just the shill at the door, Rook, and the real house is still holding all the bone cards upstairs.
SAY rook_coldwake: Then we go up and serve the notice properly. Settle down now, and remind me to draw a breath before we hit the landing.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY silas_vane: Sloping hall, grandfather clock still ticking on the landing, and a bathroom painted red from tub to tile. I don't like the odds up here, Delphine.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Don't look at the bath, darling, look in the children's room. Two little beds, a big toy chest, and a wooden doll staring from the floor.
SAY silas_vane: Leave the doll where it sits, friend. My ribs are rattling like dice in a cup, and that closet door is standing an inch ajar.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He says you're lying, and he doesn't even have eyes, Silas, you are looking right at that writhing bed in the master room.
SAY silas_vane: Nobody sleeps on a mattress that bucks like a landed pike, Delphine. Whatever paid the tab for these rooms didn't leave when the kids grew up.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY cordelia_skein: Well, Filthy Jasper has ceased his twitching on the master bed, Silas, though the linen's residual humours are still remarkably warm.
SAY silas_vane: Put a chalk mark inside my ribs for the ugly bastard, Cordelia, and don't ask me to touch that mattress while the floorboards are still humming.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do hold still, this will only tingle. Your pulse would be racing if you had one, darling, and the grandfather clock is ticking half a beat faster.
SAY silas_vane: House always wins, unless you burn the house, and we just cleared the big table only to find the walls still sweating cold grease.
SAY cordelia_skein: Quite so, the pathology of this floor was merely using him as a vessel. See how the two small beds in the nursery room haven't settled an inch.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, Cordelia, observe the taxidermy in this trophy room. That large brown bear has turned its head toward the door, and its posture is appalling.
SAY cordelia_skein: Never mind the bear, Lucan, inspect the mahogany crib and the cradle in the nursery. Both are riddled with tiny, uniform perforations, like a beetle assay.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Prime specimen of a scholarly library gone to seed, too, if you please, with a draft coming straight through walls that ought to be solid stone.
SAY cordelia_skein: That wind is descending from the ceiling over the hearth, darling. Notice the stain in the plaster, it has a square seam cut far too neatly.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Dreadfang is growling at the lectern, Cordelia, and my ears are flat back. Whatever nests above that square seam is no gentleman of the hunt.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY rook_coldwake: Mind the turf, Delphine, the floorboards past this warded door are carpeted with loose teeth. Gross violation of parish sanitation, and terrible underfoot.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Teeth I can step over, Rook, it is the six empty circles cut into the landing and that cauldron of red soup that ruin the billing.
SAY rook_coldwake: Hot copper and wet fur in the rafters, and the beams are scratched raw. My knuckles are going soft just standing in the steam.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look by the cauldron, darling, Phillip and Adela are bound tight to the floor. Keep your shield up, if anything reaches for my threads, we burn the roof.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY rook_coldwake: Well now, Vessla Browntooth is off the shift log, and the manor walls have squared themselves up straight. Decent plumb line on the porch again.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Indeed, Rook, the storm has broken over the hill road, and the air by the well tastes of clean rain rather than sour cellar rot.
SAY rook_coldwake: Two barns still leaning a touch, and the drainage round that black pond wants ditching, though at least the front door hangs true on its hinges.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Dreadfang has sat down properly by the porch steps, if you please. A seven out of ten for the estate's recovery, once the mud dries.
SAY rook_coldwake: Best chalk a breath in the ledger while the night is quiet, Lucan. One docket cleared, and a whole valley of unsealed stone waiting below.
